transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Um, I guess what brings me in is this feeling like I just can’t settle in my own body anymore. Like if I’m supposed to sit quietly and deal with paperwork, or go over household plans with someone—bills, schedules, that kind of thing—I feel like I’m crawling out of my skin.

And it sounds silly because it’s just sitting, right? Like everyone has to do forms and calendars and all that. I used to try to make these nice little folders, actually—color-coded tabs and everything—but then I’d be sitting there and just feel this pressure to get up or move or do anything else. So… yeah, that’s the main reason I’m here.
When that happens, do you feel a strong physical urge to move your body?

Yes—yeah, that’s exactly it. It feels physical, like I can’t quite settle in my own body. Especially if I’m supposed to just sit there quietly with paperwork or talk through household plans, like bills or schedules. I start feeling like I need to get up, shift around, do something else… even if there’s no real reason to.
When that feeling starts, does moving around make it go away?

Sometimes, yeah… I mean, it’s not like it magically fixes it, but I feel this pressure to get up or shift around when I’m supposed to be sitting quietly with paperwork or going over household stuff, like schedules or bills.

It’s funny, because I’ll think, “Okay, I’m going to sit down and be organized,” and then suddenly I’m up looking for a pen or moving papers around, and then I remember the laundry or something completely unrelated. But the main thing is that I just can’t seem to settle in my body when I’m meant to stay put.
Does this restless feeling also happen when you’re just sitting still doing something relaxing, like watching a movie?

I think it’s more when I’m supposed to be sitting still for something I have to handle, like paperwork or talking through bills and schedules. That’s when I really notice it—like I can’t settle in my own body.

With a movie, I mean… sometimes I’ll shift around, but I’m not sure that’s the same thing. It’s more that “I need to get up” feeling when I’m trying to do those household planning things.
When this happens, is the feeling mainly in your legs?

Not just my legs, no. I mean, I’ll move my legs sometimes, but the bigger thing is more whole-body, like I can’t settle in myself. It comes up most when I’m supposed to sit quietly and deal with paperwork or go over household plans, and then I start shifting around or wanting to get up. It’s not really like a leg feeling specifically.
When you try to do paperwork or planning, do you find your mind drifting off even when you want to stay focused?

Yeah, definitely. I’ll sit down with, like, a planning email or even a chapter of a book, and at first I think I’m reading it, I’m doing fine. And then a few minutes later I realize I’ve been staring at the same paragraph and none of it actually went in.

It’s like my eyes are still moving, but my brain has wandered off somewhere else. Sometimes I’ll go back and reread it, and then I’m annoyed because I thought I was focusing.
Did you have these kinds of focus and restlessness problems when you were a child?

Yeah… looking back, I think it was already there when I was little. Like in elementary school, I was the kid with the totally messy desk, papers crammed everywhere, and I’d forget permission slips all the time.

And teachers would send notes home saying I talked when I wasn’t supposed to, or that I couldn’t stay in my seat. I remember my mom getting those notes and being frustrated, and—sorry, this is random—but I can still picture this one folder I had that was just destroyed by the end of the year. So yes, it wasn’t just an adult thing.
Have these focus and restlessness problems caused significant trouble in your work, school, or relationships?

Yeah, it has. I mean, I’m not working right now, but at home and with volunteer stuff, it’s caused problems. People can’t really count on me the way they should be able to, because I’ll forget something or not finish it, even when I really meant to.

And then I feel awful, because I’ll have all these intentions—like I even bought this planner once with color-coded tabs, and I was so convinced that was going to fix everything—but anyway, the result is I’ve had to step back from some responsibilities. Not because I don’t care, but because things keep falling through.
When you sit down to do paperwork or planning, do you find yourself getting caught up in worry?

I’m not sure it’s worry exactly. I mean, sometimes I’ll get frustrated with it, but when I sit down to do paperwork or planning it’s more like… I just kind of lose the thread.

Like I’ll open something and then suddenly I’m thinking about whether I replied to someone’s text, or I notice a pile of laundry, or I remember this weird thing I needed to look up—sorry, that’s not really what you asked. But no, I don’t think I’d describe it as getting caught up in worry, at least not most of the time.
